Consult Summary:
- Adult male presents with 6 weeks of generalized aching and fatigue following travel to the United States, with history of a transient calf rash; clinician plans blood tests including Lyme disease serology and routine labs, with follow-up by phone.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Generalized aching (shoulders, back, hips, knees) and persistent fatigue/low energy for ~6 weeks.
- Timeline:
  - Last felt well around Christmas/New Year.
  - Traveled to the United States late January/early February; symptoms began approximately 2 weeks after return.
  - Transient rash on posterior calf noticed mid-to-late February; faded over ~2 weeks.
- Rash details:
  - Location: Back of calf.
  - Onset: Mid to late February.
  - Course: Minimal itching; resolved over a couple of weeks.
  - Possible mild fever and sore throat around that time.
  - No current rash.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Decreased appetite/early satiety; no reported weight change.
  - Daytime tiredness and reduced concentration at work.
  - Decreased exercise participation.
  - Headache “maybe” in context of feeling unwell.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No persistent cold symptoms, earache, sore throat currently, cough, shortness of breath, or phlegm.
  - No chest pain.
  - No dysphagia, reflux, or abdominal pain.
  - No diarrhea, vomiting, or blood in stools; no change in bowel habits.
  - No urinary symptoms or hematuria.
  - No joint swelling.
  - No neurological symptoms (no blurred vision, tingling, numbness).
  - Mood/stress: Currently good; no mental health concerns reported.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not specified.
- Functional impact: Continues to work (health technology), but feels less effective due to fatigue.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma:
  - Control: Reported well controlled; no recent flare-ups.
  - Medications: Using a preventive inhaler morning and night (name/dose/route/frequency not fully documented; patient reports regular use).
  - Rescue inhaler: Not clearly documented; patient indicated not using “the …” (likely reliever), details not documented.
- Hay fever (allergic rhinitis):
  - Medication: Over-the-counter antihistamine (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).

Social History:
- Occupation: Works for a health technology company.
- Living situation: Lives with wife.
- Travel: United States (late Jan/early Feb); active with walking; wore shorts and boots; does not recall any insect/tick bites.
- Tobacco: Smoking status not documented.
- Alcohol: Occasional use.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.

Investigations:
- None completed during the consult.
- Planned:
  - Blood tests: Liver function, kidney function, and complete blood count.
  - Lyme disease serology (given history of transient rash and timing post-travel/walking exposure).
  - Additional tests for causes of reduced energy/tiredness were mentioned but not specified.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Unexplained fatigue and generalized aches for 6 weeks
  - Assessment: Persistent fatigue and myalgias without red flags; decreased appetite but no weight loss; normal ROS otherwise. Impacting work and exercise.
  - Plan:
    - Order blood tests: CBC, renal and liver panels.
    - Arrange follow-up approximately 1 week after tests (telephone acceptable).
- Issue 2: Possible Lyme disease
  - Assessment: History of transient calf rash after outdoor activity and travel; no known tick bite; timing fits. Differential includes Lyme disease.
  - Plan:
    - Order Lyme disease serology.
    - If positive, initiate appropriate antibiotic therapy (specific regimen not discussed in consult).
- Issue 3: Asthma, stable
  - Assessment: No recent exacerbations; reports using preventive inhaler regularly.
  - Plan:
    - Continue current asthma regimen.
    - No changes made during this consult.

- General plan items:
  - Patient to book labs through support line.
  - Schedule phone follow-up ~1 week after completing labs to review results and next steps.

Quality checks:
- Missing/expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Full medication reconciliation (names/doses/routes/frequencies) incomplete.
  - Smoking status not documented.
  - Family history not obtained.
  - Vitals and physical examination not documented.
  - Detailed description of rash morphology not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Inhaler use: Patient initially implied not using preventive inhaler, then stated using it morning and night; conflict noted.
  - Alcohol history briefly unclear (doctor said “No,” patient then clarified “occasionally”); final interpretation: occasional alcohol use.
- Transcript quality: Minor audio dropouts/interruptions and incomplete phrases; overall history obtainable but some details unclear.
